comment: The region-pin high-water mark. PLAN.md 30.1, C157. A pin is debt: verify:sprint30 FAILS when this number goes up, so adding one is a deliberate edit to a checked-in figure rather than a drift. Routing a module lowers it. Measured statically by scripts/_region-pins.ts, never by a runtime registry.
raisedInSprint56: 🔴 Two raises recorded here at once, and the first one is an admission. 85 to 86 happened in SPRINT 48, which added a fifth pin to app/join/[token]/actions.ts and never touched this file, so verify:sprint30 has been failing on main ever since and the sprint 48 report did not say so. The ratchet worked; the person running it did not run it. 86 to 87 is sprint 56's own: lib/data/assessments.ts is pinned because assessment surfaces are not region-threaded yet, the same reason the other fifty modules under lib are. Both are debt and both are now legible.
raisedInSprint76: 🔴 87 to 88, one call site and no new file. `setSessionMinimised` is the sixth pinned call in app/join/[token]/actions.ts, which is where the patient's join flow already keeps five: submitJoin, answerConsent, checkJoinState, stopRecording and resumeAfterPayment all pin for the same reason, which is that a guest holding a link has no entity in hand for 30.x to thread. Threading a region for this one action alone would make it different from its five neighbours for no gain and would still leave the file pinned, so the file count is unchanged at 83. It is debt and it is legible, which is the whole point of this number.
raisedInSprint76b: 🔴 88 to 89, and one new FILE, 83 to 84. `lib/notify/index.ts` pins, because `record()` writes a delivery attempt and a recipient is a phone number and an address, neither of which names a region. It was added in the commit before this one and THAT COMMIT DID NOT RAISE THIS NUMBER, so verify:sprint30 and verify:sprint37r were both red on main and the commit message said nothing about it. Exactly the sprint 48 failure this file already records one paragraph up: the ratchet worked, the person did not run it. Found by the triple check, which is what a triple check is for.
